newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS- Argos eyes better H2 as profits slip.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS- Argos eyes better H2 as profits slip.

text.p: British catalogue retailer Argos Plc turned in lower first half profits as expected on Monday and said markets would be tough in the second half but it should still give a strong performance and good growth.

Argos, which has over 400 catalogue showrooms around Britain, said pretax profits for the 24 weeks ending June 14 were 28.1 million pounds ($45.3 million), down from 31.8 million previously but within expectations, and paid out an interim dividend of 6.1 pence, up 15 percent.

It said same store sales since the end of the first half were up eight percent but chairman Sir Richard Lloyd said in a statement that "the current buoyancy in consumer confidence and overall retail sales may not be sustainable."

Argos chief executive Mike Smith said higher interest rates, up one percentage point since May, could dampen spending, while consumers might stop spending windfall gains from building society conversions which had buoyed retailers in May and June.

"Our markets, we believe, are going to be tough through the remainder of the year...we're not planning for (sales growth) to be as strong as (current levels) thought the remainder of the year," Smith told Reuters.
Toys, small electrical goods and jewellery account for some 50 percent of sales at Argos.

But Smith added that Argos still expects its second half to be stronger than the same period a year ago, helped by new store openings and aggressive pricing in its catalogue, where 98 percent of goods included from its spring and summer range will be at the same price or lower.
Smith also cited planned strong advertising and an increase of just over four percent in the group's range as factors which could help second half performance.
"The group is well positioned to demonstrate continued growth in the year 1997 as a whole," Lloyd said.
Shares eased 4.5 pence to 618.5 pence as the overall market fell, with the figures largely in line with expectations.
"It's a reasonable set of figures. The reasons why the profit went down were well flagged," said BZW analyst Tony Shiret.

Argos said in May that profits for the first half were unlikely to match the year earlier period, reflecting additional costs and an adverse impact on interest income of around three million pounds arising from payment of last year's special dividend.
The group is expecting gross margin to be 0.5 percent lower in the second half, but this will not all be due to lower prices, Smith said.
Part of the decrease could come as a result of a less favourable product mix, with more spending expected on lower margin items than in the year earlier.
Smith said the company expected to open a net 29 new stores this year, increasing its total number of outlets to 433.
He said growth could also come from expanding the group's range and that if stock turn targets were met in the next four to five years, the range could go up to 11,000 products from a current 8,500.
He said that figure did not include a move into any markets in which Argos was not already active and that such a move was not a priority.
"It's all about deepening the range in the markets we're currently in," he said.
Smith added that expansion plans in Holland were on schedule but there were currently no immediate plans to expand further into continental Europe.
But he added that the company's new development division would be looking at other European opportunities, depending on progress in Holland. ($ = 0.620 British Pounds)
